title: RBAC: roles, bindings and service accounts

videos.script: Every request to the API server answers two questions before it does anything. Who is asking? And may they do this? {{two}} Until now the answer to both was easy. You were the cluster's administrator, and the administrator may do everything. {{admin}} A deploy pipeline should not be. Neither should a monitoring agent, or a colleague who only needs to read logs. {{others}} Kubernetes refuses by default. Access exists only where a rule grants it, and a rule is two objects. A Role lists what may be done. A RoleBinding says who may do it. {{objects}} You will create an identity for a pipeline, watch it be refused, grant it exactly what it needs, and then find its token inside a running pod. {{plan}}
